steps.text: A carved, gilded oval frame.

149919.file: Unidentified artist, American, 18th century - George Jaffrey II - 1999.503 - Museum of Fine Arts.jpg

steps.title: First look
steps.text: George Jaffrey, about 1715, by an unknown American artist. Compare him with the other George Jaffrey, painted about ten years earlier.

steps.title: The face
steps.text: Younger, with rosy cheeks and a slight smile.

steps.title: The wig
steps.text: A tall, dark curled wig.

steps.title: The cravat
steps.text: A white cravat, simpler than the other portrait’s lace.

steps.title: The hand
steps.text: Hand on his chest.

31483.file: Frederic Porter Vinton - La Blanchisseuse - 13.554 - Museum of Fine Arts.jpg

steps.title: First look
steps.text: A washerwoman at a stream, 1890, by Frederic Porter Vinton, a Boston portrait painter, here working loosely, in the open air.

steps.title: The washerwoman
steps.text: She bends over the water, scrubbing clothes on a stone.

steps.title: Another figure
steps.text: Behind her, another woman stands at a wooden rail.

steps.title: The stones
steps.text: Flat washing stones at the water’s edge.

steps.title: The water
steps.text: Broken strokes of green and white make the reflections shimmer.

steps.title: Sun and shade
steps.text: Bright sunlight through the leaves.

31071.file: George de Forest Brush - Mother and Child - 95.1375 - Museum of Fine Arts.jpg

steps.title: First look
steps.text: Mother and Child, 1895. George de Forest Brush often painted his wife and children like this.

steps.title: The faces
steps.text: Mother and child cheek to cheek, looking in different directions.

steps.title: The child
steps.text: The child’s pale body glows against the mother’s dark dress.

steps.title: The hands
steps.text: Her hand holds the child’s legs.

steps.title: The feet
steps.text: Small bare feet dangle at the bottom.

steps.title: The round shape
steps.text: A round painting, like a Renaissance Madonna and Child. Brush admired the old masters.

31921.file: George Fuller - Negro Funeral, Alabama - 21.2174 - Museum of Fine Arts.jpg

steps.title: First look
steps.text: A funeral in Alabama, painted in 1881 by George Fuller, who traveled through the South in 1858. The title uses the language of its time.

steps.title: The mourners
steps.text: A crowd gathered in the open, in dim, smoky light.

steps.title: Raised arms
steps.text: A figure raises its arms, perhaps a preacher.

steps.title: The tree
steps.text: A thin tree stands alone in the middle.

steps.title: The golden haze
steps.text: Fuller blurs everything in a warm, misty glow, like a memory.

steps.title: The ground
steps.text: A dark, empty foreground.

31550.file: George Henry Boughton - Sea Breeze - 16.67 - Museum of Fine Arts.jpg

steps.title: First look
steps.text: A young woman by the sea, by George Henry Boughton, who grew up in Albany, New York, and later worked in London.

steps.title: The hat
steps.text: A straw hat with a red flower and white ribbons.

steps.title: The breeze
steps.text: Her scarf and ribbons blow in the wind from the sea.

steps.title: The flower
steps.text: She holds a red flower on the stone wall.

steps.title: The harbor
steps.text: A lighthouse and ships far behind her.

steps.title: The pink dress
steps.text: Soft pinks against the deep blue water.

31545.file: George Henry Hall - Roman Wine Cart - 16.44 - Museum of Fine Arts.jpg

steps.title: First look
steps.text: A wine cart on its way into Rome, painted in 1851 by George Henry Hall, an American who studied in Europe.

steps.title: The woman
steps.text: She smiles at us, holding a tambourine.

steps.title: The driver
steps.text: A bearded man sits close beside her.

steps.title: The hood
steps.text: A folding hood shades the driver’s seat.

steps.title: The Colosseum
steps.text: The Colosseum on the left tells us we are in Rome.

steps.title: The wheel
steps.text: A big wooden wheel at the bottom left.

31929.file: John Singer Sargent - Ganymede and the Eagle - 21.10508 - Museum of Fine Arts.jpg

steps.title: First look
steps.text: Look up! John Singer Sargent decorated the Rotunda between 1916 and 1921. He designed the plaster reliefs around the paintings too. Here: Zeus, as an eagle, carries off the Trojan boy Ganymede to serve the gods.

steps.title: The eagle
steps.text: Huge wings fill the circle; the boy hangs on, swept up into the sky.

steps.title: The reliefs above
steps.text: Sculpted figures sit on top of the frame, in white plaster.

steps.title: Below
steps.text: More winged figures in relief at the bottom.

steps.title: Paint and plaster
steps.text: The paintings are oil on canvas, glued to the ceiling like wallpaper.

31930.file: John Singer Sargent - Music - 21.10509 - Museum of Fine Arts.jpg

steps.title: First look
steps.text: Look up! John Singer Sargent decorated the Rotunda between 1916 and 1921. He designed the plaster reliefs around the paintings too. This roundel is Music.

steps.title: The violinist
steps.text: A woman in white plays the violin, head thrown back.

steps.title: The bow
steps.text: Follow the bow across the strings.

steps.title: The reliefs
steps.text: Two sculpted figures recline on top of the frame.

steps.title: Below
steps.text: Another relief: a figure stretching out.

31931.file: John Singer Sargent - Astronomy - 21.10510 - Museum of Fine Arts.jpg

steps.title: First look
steps.text: Look up! John Singer Sargent decorated the Rotunda between 1916 and 1921. He designed the plaster reliefs around the paintings too. This roundel is Astronomy.

steps.title: The figure
steps.text: A seated figure, wrapped in robes, looks out into the dark.

steps.title: The reliefs
steps.text: Plaster figures sit on top of the frame.

steps.title: Paint and plaster
steps.text: The paintings are oil on canvas, glued to the ceiling like wallpaper.

31932.file: John Singer Sargent - Prometheus - 21.10511 - Museum of Fine Arts.jpg

steps.title: First look
steps.text: Look up! John Singer Sargent decorated the Rotunda between 1916 and 1921. He designed the plaster reliefs around the paintings too. Prometheus stole fire for humans; as punishment, Zeus sent an eagle to attack him every day.

steps.title: The eagle
steps.text: Dark wings spread over the twisted body of Prometheus.

steps.title: The reliefs
steps.text: Sculpted figures above the frame.

steps.title: The archer
steps.text: At the bottom, a relief of an archer drawing his bow.

steps.title: First look
steps.text: Look up! John Singer Sargent decorated the Rotunda between 1916 and 1921. He designed the plaster reliefs around the paintings too. Apollo, god of music and poetry, with the nine Muses, goddesses of the arts.

steps.title: Apollo
steps.text: In the center, with a halo of light behind his head.

steps.title: The Muses
steps.text: They dance around him in a ring, robes swirling.

steps.title: The masks
steps.text: Theater masks in the corners of the frame.

31934.file: John Singer Sargent - Architecture, Painting and Sculpture Protected by Athena from the Ravages of Time - 21.10513 - Museum of Fine Arts.jpg

steps.title: First look
steps.text: Look up! John Singer Sargent decorated the Rotunda between 1916 and 1921. He designed the plaster reliefs around the paintings too. The full title: Architecture, Painting and Sculpture Protected by Athena from the Ravages of Time.

steps.title: Athena
steps.text: The goddess of wisdom, in her helmet, watches over them.

steps.title: The three arts
steps.text: Three women sit together: Architecture, Painting and Sculpture.

steps.title: The inscription
steps.text: Their names in Latin: ARCHITECTVRA, PICTVRA, SCVLPTVRA.

31935.file: John Singer Sargent - Classic and Romantic Art - 21.10514 - Museum of Fine Arts.jpg

steps.title: First look
steps.text: Look up! John Singer Sargent decorated the Rotunda between 1916 and 1921. He designed the plaster reliefs around the paintings too. Classic and Romantic Art: two kinds of art, with Apollo between them.

steps.title: Apollo
steps.text: In the center, rays of light burst out behind him.

steps.title: The left side
steps.text: A wilder group, with a leopard.

steps.title: The right side
steps.text: A calmer group, elegant and composed.

steps.title: The swans
steps.text: Swans at Apollo’s feet: swans were sacred to him.

31936.file: John Singer Sargent - The Sphinx and the Chimaera - 21.10515 - Museum of Fine Arts.jpg

steps.title: First look
steps.text: Look up! John Singer Sargent decorated the Rotunda between 1916 and 1921. He designed the plaster reliefs around the paintings too. Two monsters of myth: the Sphinx, who asked riddles, and the winged Chimaera.

steps.title: The Sphinx
steps.text: Her calm stone face, eyes half closed.

steps.title: The Chimaera
steps.text: The winged creature swoops down to her.

steps.title: The inscription
steps.text: THE SPHINX AND THE CHIMAERA

32212.file: John Singer Sargent - The Danaïdes - 25.636 - Museum of Fine Arts.jpg

steps.title: First look
steps.text: Look up! Sargent painted these for the Colonnade and the stair between 1922 and 1925. He died in 1925, just before the last ones went up. The Danaïdes killed their husbands on their wedding night. Their punishment in the underworld: fill a leaking jar, forever.

steps.title: The women
steps.text: One after another they bring water, jars on their shoulders.

steps.title: The great jar
steps.text: The jar they can never fill.

32216.file: Sargent - Apollo in His Chariot with the Hours, 1922–25, 25.640.jpg

steps.title: First look
steps.text: Look up! Sargent painted these for the Colonnade and the stair between 1922 and 1925. He died in 1925, just before the last ones went up. Apollo, the sun god, drives his chariot across the sky, with the Hours dancing around it.

steps.title: Apollo
steps.text: He leans forward, holding the reins.

steps.title: The horses
steps.text: White horses charge ahead.

steps.title: The Hours
steps.text: Dancing figures circle the chariot: the hours of the day.

steps.title: The wheel
steps.text: The great wheel of the chariot.

steps.title: First look
steps.text: Look up! Sargent painted these for the Colonnade and the stair between 1922 and 1925. He died in 1925, just before the last ones went up. The Winds: figures rush through the clouds.

steps.title: The dark figure
steps.text: A figure wrapped in a dark cloak dives down through the sky.

steps.title: The flowers
steps.text: Flowers scatter on the right, blown by a gentler wind.

steps.title: The clouds
steps.text: Soft pink clouds on both sides.

32218.file: John Singer Sargent - Perseus on Pegasus Slaying Medusa - 25.642 - Museum of Fine Arts.jpg

steps.title: First look
steps.text: Look up! Sargent painted these for the Colonnade and the stair between 1922 and 1925. He died in 1925, just before the last ones went up. Perseus cut off the head of Medusa, whose gaze turned people to stone.

steps.title: Perseus on Pegasus
steps.text: The hero rides the winged horse.

steps.title: Medusa’s head
steps.text: He holds up the head, with snakes for hair.

steps.title: Athena
steps.text: The goddess Athena helped him.

steps.title: Medusa’s body
steps.text: Below, her body lies among the clouds.

32219.file: John Singer Sargent - Atlas and the Hesperides, 1922-1925.jpg

steps.title: First look
steps.text: Look up! Sargent painted these for the Colonnade and the stair between 1922 and 1925. He died in 1925, just before the last ones went up. Atlas holds up the sky while the Hesperides, nymphs who guarded the golden apples, sleep.

steps.title: Atlas
steps.text: Bent forward, the whole sky on his back.

steps.title: The stars
steps.text: Stars on the dark dome above him.

steps.title: The Hesperides
steps.text: They sleep in a tangle at his feet.

steps.title: First look
steps.text: Look up! Sargent painted these for the Colonnade and the stair between 1922 and 1925. He died in 1925, just before the last ones went up. The centaur Chiron, half man and half horse, was the teacher of the hero Achilles.

steps.title: Chiron
steps.text: The centaur gallops through the clouds.

steps.title: Achilles
steps.text: The young hero rides on his back, drawing a bow.

steps.title: The eagle
steps.text: An eagle in the corner: a target for the lesson?

steps.title: First look
steps.text: Look up! Sargent painted these for the Colonnade and the stair between 1922 and 1925. He died in 1925, just before the last ones went up. Orestes killed his mother to avenge his father. The Furies, spirits of revenge, chase him.

steps.title: Orestes
steps.text: He runs, arms up to shield himself.

steps.title: The Furies
steps.text: Snakes in their hair, torches in their hands.

steps.title: The signature
steps.text: Bottom right: JOHN S. SARGENT.

32222.file: John Singer Sargent - Phaethon - 25.646 - Museum of Fine Arts.jpg

steps.title: First look
steps.text: Look up! Sargent painted these for the Colonnade and the stair between 1922 and 1925. He died in 1925, just before the last ones went up. Phaethon, son of the sun god, borrowed his father’s chariot, lost control, and was struck down by Zeus.

steps.title: The fall
steps.text: Phaethon tumbles head first.

steps.title: The scorpion
steps.text: A giant scorpion at the top. In Ovid’s telling, the Scorpion of the zodiac terrified the horses.

steps.title: The beam
steps.text: A great diagonal beam cuts across the circle.

steps.title: First look
steps.text: Look up! Sargent painted these for the Colonnade and the stair between 1922 and 1925. He died in 1925, just before the last ones went up. Hercules fights the Hydra, a serpent whose heads grew back when cut off.

steps.title: Hercules
steps.text: Club raised over his head.

steps.title: The heads
steps.text: Heads everywhere, mouths open.

steps.title: The flames
steps.text: Look at the flames at the necks: fire stopped new heads from growing.

steps.title: The coils
steps.text: The serpent’s body knots around his legs.
